y1-pl-1.o: Identify and name a variety of common wild and garden plants, including deciduous and evergreen trees

y1-pl-2.o: Identify and describe the basic structure of a variety of common flowering plants, including trees

y1-an-1.o: Identify and name a variety of common animals including fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals

y1-an-2.o: Identify and name a variety of common animals that are carnivores, herbivores and omnivores

y1-an-3.o: Describe and compare the structure of a variety of common animals (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals, including pets)

y1-an-4.o: Identify, name, draw and label the basic parts of the human body and say which part of the body is associated with each sense

y1-ma-1.o: Distinguish between an object and the material from which it is made

y1-ma-2.o: Identify and name a variety of everyday materials, including wood, plastic, glass, metal, water, and rock

y1-ma-3.o: Describe the simple physical properties of a variety of everyday materials

y1-ma-4.o: Compare and group together a variety of everyday materials on the basis of their simple physical properties

y1-se-1.o: Observe changes across the four seasons

y1-se-2.o: Observe and describe weather associated with the seasons and how day length varies

y2-lh-1.o: Explore and compare the differences between things that are living, dead, and things that have never been alive

y2-lh-2.o: Identify that most living things live in habitats to which they are suited and describe how different habitats provide for the basic needs of different kinds of animals and plants, and how they depend on each other

y2-lh-3.o: Identify and name a variety of plants and animals in their habitats, including micro-habitats

y2-lh-4.o: Describe how animals obtain their food from plants and other animals, using the idea of a simple food chain, and identify and name different sources of food

y2-pl-1.o: Observe and describe how seeds and bulbs grow into mature plants

y2-pl-2.o: Find out and describe how plants need water, light and a suitable temperature to grow and stay healthy

y2-an-1.o: Notice that animals, including humans, have offspring which grow into adults

y2-an-2.o: Find out about and describe the basic needs of animals, including humans, for survival (water, food and air)

y2-an-3.o: Describe the importance for humans of exercise, eating the right amounts of different types of food, and hygiene

y2-ma-1.o: Identify and compare the suitability of a variety of everyday materials, including wood, metal, plastic, glass, brick, rock, paper and cardboard for particular uses

y2-ma-2.o: Find out how the shapes of solid objects made from some materials can be changed by squashing, bending, twisting and stretching

y3-pl-1.o: Identify and describe the functions of different parts of flowering plants: roots, stem/trunk, leaves and flowers

y3-pl-2.o: Explore the requirements of plants for life and growth (air, light, water, nutrients from soil, and room to grow) and how they vary from plant to plant

y3-pl-3.o: Investigate the way in which water is transported within plants

y3-pl-4.o: Explore the part that flowers play in the life cycle of flowering plants, including pollination, seed formation and seed dispersal

y3-an-1.o: Identify that animals, including humans, need the right types and amount of nutrition, and that they cannot make their own food; they get nutrition from what they eat

y3-an-2.o: Identify that humans and some other animals have skeletons and muscles for support, protection and movement

y3-ro-1.o: Compare and group together different kinds of rocks on the basis of their appearance and simple physical properties

y3-ro-2.o: Describe in simple terms how fossils are formed when things that have lived are trapped within rock

y3-ro-3.o: Recognise that soils are made from rocks and organic matter

y3-li-1.o: Recognise that they need light in order to see things and that dark is the absence of light

y3-li-2.o: Notice that light is reflected from surfaces

y3-li-3.o: Recognise that light from the sun can be dangerous and that there are ways to protect their eyes

y3-li-4.o: Recognise that shadows are formed when the light from a light source is blocked by an opaque object

y3-li-5.o: Find patterns in the way that the size of shadows change

y3-fo-1.o: Compare how things move on different surfaces

y3-fo-2.o: Notice that some forces need contact between two objects, but magnetic forces can act at a distance

y3-fo-3.o: Observe how magnets attract or repel each other and attract some materials and not others

y3-fo-4.o: Describe magnets as having two poles

y3-fo-5.o: Predict whether two magnets will attract or repel each other, depending on which poles are facing

y4-lv-1.o: Recognise that living things can be grouped in a variety of ways

y4-lv-2.o: Explore and use classification keys to help group, identify and name a variety of living things in their local and wider environment

y4-lv-3.o: Recognise that environments can change and that this can sometimes pose dangers to living things

y4-an-1.o: Describe the simple functions of the basic parts of the digestive system in humans

y4-an-2.o: Identify the different types of teeth in humans and their simple functions

y4-an-3.o: Construct and interpret a variety of food chains, identifying producers, predators and prey

y4-st-1.o: Compare and group materials together, according to whether they are solids, liquids or gases

y4-st-2.o: Observe that some materials change state when they are heated or cooled, and measure or research the temperature at which this happens in degrees Celsius (°C)

y4-st-3.o: Identify the part played by evaporation and condensation in the water cycle and associate the rate of evaporation with temperature

y4-sd-1.o: Identify how sounds are made, associating some of them with something vibrating

y4-sd-2.o: Recognise that vibrations from sounds travel through a medium to the ear

y4-sd-3.o: Find patterns between the pitch of a sound and features of the object that produced it

y4-sd-4.o: Find patterns between the volume of a sound and the strength of the vibrations that produced it

y4-sd-5.o: Recognise that sounds get fainter as the distance from the sound source increases

y4-el-1.o: Identify common appliances that run on electricity

y4-el-2.o: Construct a simple series electrical circuit, identifying and naming its basic parts, including cells, wires, bulbs, switches and buzzers

y4-el-3.o: Identify whether or not a lamp will light in a simple series circuit, based on whether or not the lamp is part of a complete loop with a battery

y4-el-4.o: Recognise that a switch opens and closes a circuit and associate this with whether or not a lamp lights in a simple series circuit

y4-el-5.o: Recognise some common conductors and insulators, and associate metals with being good conductors

y5-lv-1.o: Describe the differences in the life cycles of a mammal, an amphibian, an insect and a bird

y5-lv-2.o: Describe the life process of reproduction in some plants and animals

y5-an-1.o: Describe the changes as humans develop to old age

y5-mt-1.o: Compare and group together everyday materials on the basis of their properties, including their hardness, solubility, transparency, conductivity (electrical and thermal), and response to magnets

y5-mt-2.o: Know that some materials will dissolve in liquid to form a solution, and describe how to recover a substance from a solution

y5-mt-3.o: Use knowledge of solids, liquids and gases to decide how mixtures might be separated, including through filtering, sieving and evaporating

y5-mt-4.o: Give reasons, based on evidence from comparative and fair tests, for the particular uses of everyday materials, including metals, wood and plastic

y5-mt-5.o: Demonstrate that dissolving, mixing and changes of state are reversible changes

y5-mt-6.o: Explain that some changes result in the formation of new materials, and that this kind of change is not usually reversible, including changes associated with burning and the action of acid on bicarbonate of soda

y5-es-1.o: Describe the movement of the Earth, and other planets, relative to the Sun in the solar system

y5-es-2.o: Describe the movement of the Moon relative to the Earth

y5-es-3.o: Describe the Sun, Earth and Moon as approximately spherical bodies

y5-es-4.o: Use the idea of the Earth’s rotation to explain day and night and the apparent movement of the sun across the sky

y5-fo-1.o: Explain that unsupported objects fall towards the Earth because of the force of gravity acting between the Earth and the falling object

y5-fo-2.o: Identify the effects of air resistance, water resistance and friction, that act between moving surfaces

y5-fo-3.o: Recognise that some mechanisms, including levers, pulleys and gears, allow a smaller force to have a greater effect

y6-lv-1.o: Describe how living things are classified into broad groups according to common observable characteristics and based on similarities and differences, including micro-organisms, plants and animals

y6-lv-2.o: Give reasons for classifying plants and animals based on specific characteristics

y6-an-1.o: Identify and name the main parts of the human circulatory system, and describe the functions of the heart, blood vessels and blood

y6-an-2.o: Recognise the impact of diet, exercise, drugs and lifestyle on the way their bodies function

y6-an-3.o: Describe the ways in which nutrients and water are transported within animals, including humans

y6-ev-1.o: Recognise that living things have changed over time and that fossils provide information about living things that inhabited the Earth millions of years ago

y6-ev-2.o: Recognise that living things produce offspring of the same kind, but normally offspring vary and are not identical to their parents

y6-ev-3.o: Identify how animals and plants are adapted to suit their environment in different ways and that adaptation may lead to evolution

y6-lt-1.o: Recognise that light appears to travel in straight lines

y6-lt-2.o: Use the idea that light travels in straight lines to explain that objects are seen because they give out or reflect light into the eye

y6-lt-3.o: Explain that we see things because light travels from light sources to our eyes or from light sources to objects and then to our eyes

y6-lt-4.o: Use the idea that light travels in straight lines to explain why shadows have the same shape as the objects that cast them

y6-el-1.o: Associate the brightness of a lamp or the volume of a buzzer with the number and voltage of cells used in the circuit

y6-el-2.o: Compare and give reasons for variations in how components function, including the brightness of bulbs, the loudness of buzzers and the on/off position of switches

y6-el-3.o: Use recognised symbols when representing a simple circuit in a diagram
